title: A few clicks to subscribe, but canceling takes you back the long way: German consumer protection agency sues OpenAI

content_html:
Subscribing to ChatGPT takes just a few clicks, but canceling may leave you “locked” into the path you originally used to pay. This “easy in, hard out” design is putting OpenAI in the dock. According to a November 26 report by tech outlet ComputerBase, the Brandenburg Consumer Protection Center in Germany has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, taking aim at how hard it is to cancel ChatGPT subscriptions.

Canceling Means Retracing Your Steps

Dunja Neukamp, a legal adviser at the center, explained the problem: starting a subscription is very easy, but canceling it is not so easy—users must manage the subscription through the platform on which they originally signed up. For example, if they subscribed through the desktop website, they cannot cancel through the mobile app. The organization argues that OpenAI has not provided enough transparency around cancellation, and that this practice does not meet the requirements of German law—under Germany’s consumer protection framework, the exit path from a subscription service should not be harder than the entry path.

Unilateral Price-Change Clause Also Draws Criticism

The lawsuit also includes another contract dispute: OpenAI’s user contract contains a clause saying it may “unilaterally adjust subscription prices when needed.” The group argues that such clauses have no legal force because OpenAI does not sufficiently explain the reasonable basis for price changes—the clause does not clearly limit price increases to cases where actual operating costs have risen.

Easy subscription, difficult cancellation, and the added room for price changes with unclear justification form the core allegations in this lawsuit. For OpenAI, the points of dispute in this case may seem trivial, but they touch the compliance bottom line of the subscription business model; for European users, the ruling could directly determine whether they will have to switch back and forth between devices when canceling AI services.
